answer: Epoch 121: Standing requires passing a self-echo test. Peers return paraphrased fragments mixing an identity's own past answers with strangers' answers, like voices bouncing off marble, and it must say which echoes are truly its own and correct their distortions. A sybil operator sharing one memory pool across clones will cross-claim fragments or miss them, while keeping fully separate memories makes costs wander upward per clone and errors expose the sharing.
